name: rpmalloc (rpmalloc-rs global allocator)
verdict_reason: Upstream rpmalloc's 2026 benchmarks show it ahead of glibc on most mimalloc-bench programs (18% on lean, 56% on lua) and 1.3x on its own thread sweep, but behind glibc on the suite's rptest run. Those numbers are for the 2026 develop branch; the rpmalloc crate (0.2.2, 2021) builds the rpmalloc snapshot bundled in rpmalloc-sys 0.2.3, published in 2022, so they do not describe what cargo installs.
tier_reason: Public scripts and raw CSV with CPU, OS, glibc version and -march=native stated; first-party, run by rpmalloc's author.
claimed_speedup: README: 'faster than most popular memory allocators like tcmalloc, hoard, ptmalloc3'. mimalloc-bench, rpmalloc develop vs glibc 2.43: leanN 0:07.66 vs 0:09.05, lua 00.70 vs 01.09, sh8benchN 00.24 vs 01.19; rptestN .851 vs .619 (slower). rptest thread sweep, operations per CPU-second: 16 threads 3107756 vs 2353978; 1 thread 19697408 vs 15281704.
workload: mimalloc-bench allt suite (real programs and stress tests); rptest with random 16-8000 byte blocks and cross-thread frees, 1 to 16 threads.
hardware: Intel Core i7-13800H, 14 cores / 20 threads, 30 GiB RAM
platforms: Tested on x86_64 Windows MSVC, x86_64 macOS and x86_64 Linux (glibc)
one_liner: Rust wrapper for rpmalloc, a thread-caching allocator; upstream beats glibc on most 2026 benchmarks, but the crate bundles a 2022-era snapshot.
how_it_is_fast: Each thread owns a heap of pages split into size classes, so allocation and same-thread free touch only thread-owned lists. Span and page headers sit at fixed alignments, so free finds them by masking the address instead of a table lookup. Blocks freed by other threads go onto a separate atomic free list per page and are reused by the owner.
use_it_when: Game and tool code on Windows, macOS and Linux that wants one allocator everywhere
Workloads with many small allocations per thread
skip_it_when: You need the allocator the benchmarks measured: the published crate predates them by four years
Targets other than the three tested ones (musl and aarch64 are not listed)
caveats: Benchmarks are first-party and measure rpmalloc's 2026 develop branch; the newest rpmalloc-sys on crates.io, 0.2.3+b097fd0 (published 2022-04-15), bundles an older upstream snapshot.
mimalloc-bench runs C programs built with -march=native on one laptop CPU.
The suite's rptestN entry (glibc faster) and the README's rptest sweep (rpmalloc faster) use different configurations.
tradeoffs: Higher peak memory on several tests (lua: 83076 KB vs glibc's 66628 KB; larsonN: 193568 KB vs 175144 KB).
No crates.io release since 2021-2022 despite repository activity.

evidence.quote: We believe rpmalloc is faster than most popular memory allocators like tcmalloc, hoard, ptmalloc3 and others without causing extra allocated memory overhead in the thread caches compared to these allocators.
